notes:
## 0.2.160

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** `GET /image/{key}` now also accepts a device bearer token
alongside a browser session (specs/SPECWindowsClient.md §4.1), entitled through the same
subscription-derived check the session path already uses — the same credential
`GET /feeds/article/{id}/text` already accepted. No migration, no configuration key, no wire or
collection change; an existing browser session is unaffected. This is the foundation half of the
`:client` desktop reader (specs/SPECWindowsClient.md, specs/SPECClientInterface.md): a new
`:client` Gradle module holding the replica store, the pairing flow and the sync loop over
`com.mambocoding.sync:core`, plus the image/article-text fetch-and-cache this owes line covers the
server side of. It never reaches the shipped image — the `Dockerfile` builds `:server:installDist`
only — so it owes an operator nothing beyond the one route above.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** The reader gains a two-pane layout at 1280px and wider —
list and article side by side on the timeline and its five filtered views, the list keeping its
own scroll position while the article swaps beside it — plus `accesskey` accelerators on mark
read/star/save/refresh/search (`m`/`s`/`v`/`r`/`/`, specs/SPECDesktopWidth.md). Markup and CSS
only: no migration, no configuration key, no new script (the CSP's four vendored scripts are
unchanged), no wire or collection change. Admin tables and dashboard grids also stop being
crushed or unbounded at that width — auto-width tables with a per-cell minimum, and `.app-grid`
capped at four columns — and article/notes/settings prose is now capped in `ch` rather than
pixels.

owes: **a new outbound request class, and one new configuration key.** The hub now reads a
summary-only article's own full text once for the household (`specs/SPECArticleFullText.md`),
which means it dials an article's own `link` — a URL written by the feed's publisher, not typed by
this household — the same guard, dialler and sanitiser as every other fetch, with its own tighter
3-hop redirect cap and `robots.txt` honoured. Migration `V027` adds `article_text`, purged with its
article by the existing retention setting; nothing to configure to keep the previous behaviour.
`SYNCHUB_ARTICLE_TEXT_MAX_BYTES` (default 2 MiB) caps the response, live-editable like
`SYNCHUB_BLOB_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES` already is. `/data` grows with whatever full text this fetches;
Settings → Feeds now reports that store's own size beside the existing purge sentence. No wire,
collection or payload change — text is served from `GET /feeds/article/{id}/text`, never synced.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** Accounts gain roles (`admin`, `updater` — `specs/SPECRoles.md`):
migration `V026` runs automatically on startup and backfills every existing admin's `roles` to
`'admin'` from its `is_admin` flag, which stays in the table and keeps being written alongside
`roles` on every change, so a rollback to an image that only reads `is_admin` still finds its admins.
No configuration key, no wire or collection change — a role is never synced, never in a device token,
never in `GET /hub/status` beyond the same admin-only `update` field it already gated. The only
operator-visible change is in Settings → Users, where an admin can now grant `updater` alone through
a checkbox per row (`POST /admin/users/{id}/roles`) — nothing to configure, nothing to migrate by hand.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** Opening an article now marks it read automatically
(`specs/SPECReaderOpenMarksRead.md`) — a browser-visible behavior change, not an operator one: no
migration, no configuration key, and no wire or collection change beyond the existing
`feed.item_state` write path a manual read toggle already used.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** No migration, no hub configuration key, no wire or collection
change, `GET /hub/status` unchanged. The two shipped templates changed, and nothing reads them but a
`docker compose` you run yourself — but if you adopt either one, read the three lines below first.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** The notes module (specs/SPECNotesModule.md §11 phase 3) gains a
daily trash sweep and `/notes/search`. No migration, no configuration key: the sweep's own due-check
uses one new key (`notes_sweep_last_at`) in the existing `hub_state` table, and starts and stops with
the module's own toggle exactly like every other lifecycle already does. `notes.notes` records with
`deletedAt` older than 30 days are now purged automatically, once a day, whether or not a phone is
paired or online — the same tombstone a manual *Delete permanently* already wrote, and the existing
30-day grace period then removes it as usual. `docker logs` gains one `Notes: N record(s) purged for
M owner(s)` line per actual sweep.

owes: **check `volumes.synchub-data.name` before starting an existing hub on this `compose.yml`.**
It says `synchub-data` again, which is what `specs/SPECDataDurability.md` §5 specifies and what every
release up to `0.2.135` shipped. `0.2.136` through `0.2.142` shipped `name: synchub_synchub-data`
instead — one operator's own value, committed by accident — so a hub installed from one of those four
files and then started on this one looks factory-fresh, on an empty volume, with its data still
sitting under the other name. Run `docker volume ls`; then either migrate (the commands are in the
`0.1.32` entry below) or write your own name into that field, which is a supported answer and the
reason the field is explicit.

owes: **`SYNCHUB_TAG=` ships empty, and `latest` was never a valid value.** The shipped `.env`
carried `SYNCHUB_TAG=latest` under a comment saying `latest` is refused. Compose starts on it, so
nothing complains — but the launcher reads that line as a version, and when it is not one the *Apply
update* button refuses permanently and says so directly: About reads `tagNotAVersion` — *.env must
pin a version* — rather than the older, vaguer *unresolved* (`specs/SPECApplyRefusalSaysWhich.md`).
If your own `.env` says `latest`, put the number `docker ps`
shows there now; the button cannot work until you do. For a fresh install, the number comes from the
same public feed the hub and the launcher read, with no account and no token — this repository is
private, so its Releases page answers a stranger with a `404`:
`curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mambocoding/io/main/synchub/latest.json | jq -r .version`.

owes: **`SYNCHUB_TLS_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD=` is in the shipped `.env` now, empty.** It was missing while
`compose.yml` demanded it with `:?`, so the two shipped files together refused to start with no line
to fill. Fill it before the first `docker compose up -d`, and never change it afterwards — a hub
whose password no longer matches `/data/keystore.p12` refuses to start.

owes: **a fourth app, `notes`, is servable and read-only** (`specs/SPECNotesModule.md` phase 1). It
is off by default, exactly like `weather` and `stocks` were on their own first release — an operator
turns it on in Settings → Apps, with no restart, and sees the phone's notebook (list and one note)
with no ability yet to create, edit, delete, search, or manage labels/attachments from the browser;
those arrive in later phases. No migration: this module adds no table, no column and no index — it
reads the same `notes.*` records the phone has already been pushing since pairing, whether or not
this build carried the module. No configuration key, no wire or collection change.

owes: **nothing new to a running hub.** The `notes` app (still off by default) now lets a signed-in
user create, edit, delete, restore and organise their own notes from the browser
(`specs/SPECNotesModule.md` phase 2) — the list, checklists, labels, archive, trash and the app's own
settings are all writable now, and the editor keeps both copies when a browser edit and a phone push
diverge, the same as the phone does. Still no migration: every write lands in the same `notes.*`
records phase 1 already read, through the same `UserRecordStore.pushBatch` the sync endpoint uses —
no new table, no new column, no configuration key, no wire or collection change.

owes: **`feedCore`, `weatherCore`, `stocksCore` repin `0.5.10` → `0.5.14`, and `syncProtocol`/
`syncCore` repin `0.9.12` → `0.9.17`.** All five are version repins only — nothing owed to a running
hub. DataCore's `0.5.14` is a test-fixture-only change; SyncCore's `0.9.17` adds a Blob transport
seam this hub does not consume (`http/BlobRoutes.kt` implements its own local blob routes).

owes: **nothing new to a running hub.** The `notes` app (still off by default) gains attachments
(`specs/SPECNotesModule.md` §11 phase 4, §7 whole) — a photograph or file added to a note from the
browser, before the phone can. Rides the blob store `0.2.128` already shipped: no migration, no new
configuration key, `SYNCHUB_BLOB_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES` now also bounds this upload. `/data/blobs/renditions/`
is a new directory — this hub's own re-encoded PNG for an image attachment, capped at 1600px, never the
uploaded file itself — and will grow alongside `/data/blobs/` as attachments are viewed. No wire or
collection change beyond the `attachments` field `notes.notes` already carried on the wire; removing an
attachment from a note never releases the underlying blob claim, by design (§7.6) — disk from an
attachment nobody references any more is a bounded, visible cost, not a leak this hub can safely guess
at closing.

owes: the hub now removes subscription records under their pre-migration ids, one day after every
device of that owner has synced past the new ones.

owes: **nothing to a running hub, and this is new administrator power, stated plainly.** Settings
gains an admin-only *Backup* page and `POST /settings/backup/download` (`specs/SPECHubBackup.md`),
re-authenticated with the current password — and the current one-time code, when the account has a
second factor — through the existing rate limiter. This widens what an administrator could already
do: `specs/SPECSecurity.md` §2's household adversary is amended in the same commit to say so. No
migration, no configuration key, no wire or collection change — `hub_state` already had the shape
this needed for the backup count and the last archive's instant and size. The archive never contains
the TLS private key, the keystore, or `SYNCHUB_SECRET_KEY`, so a restored hub gets a new certificate
fingerprint and every paired device must re-pin — expected, not a bug. Taking a backup briefly slows
the whole hub down, since the snapshot runs through the single database connection; the page says so.

owes: **nothing verified, and that is the point of this line.** `gradle/libs.versions.toml` repins
`feedCore`/`weatherCore`/`stocksCore` (0.5.14 → 0.5.15) and `syncProtocol`/`syncCore` (0.9.17 →
0.9.18) at the human's explicit request, from this session's own pin-check hook. This repository has
no local DataCore or SyncCore checkout, so their own `specs/RELEASES.md` notes for these intervals
were **not** read here — each `gradle/libs.versions.toml` comment says so plainly. Treat this as a
version repin only until a human confirms nothing in those intervals is actually owed.
